title: openai-compat: unify tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI-compat function/tool-calling surface closer to community expectations and remove ambiguity around tool_choice semantics, while also making tool schema mapping more robust and standardizing tool->assistant message formatting.

Summary:
- Define explicit semantics for tool_choice in multi-tool scenarios (when models return a tool_choice object).
- Introduce a deterministic schema-mapping layer that converts OpenAI-style tool schemas into our internal tool descriptors, with disambiguation rules for conflicting types and optional fields.
- Normalize the formatting of messages emitted by tools (assistant role messages produced by tools) so downstream chat consumers and streaming output are consistent.
- Add end-to-end tests across the Python SDK and runtime streaming path.

Changes in this PR: single continuous description below includes design, compatibility considerations, tests, and migration notes.

Design & Implementation:
1) tool_choice semantics: we now treat tool_choice as authoritative when present in model output. If multiple tool_choice entries are present (historical models), we use the highest-confidence score with tie-breaker priority by declaration order. If model returns a bare tool name without an index, we resolve by exact name match against active catalog; ambiguous matches produce a soft error event and fall back to assistant text. The behavior is documented in the updated spec (redwood/openai_compat/spec.md).

2) Schema mapping: introduced a mapping pipeline that: (a) validates OpenAI JSON Schema fields, (b) canonicalizes type aliases (e.g., integer->number when model uses both), (c) flattens nested objects when the tool declares flattened params, and (d) emits a deterministic internal schema id. Conflicting field names across multiple tools in a single call are namespaced with the tool id to avoid accidental collisions. Mapping errors are surfaced as structured warnings in the operation trace rather than hard failures.

3) Tool message formatting: standardized the shape of messages created by tools before they re-enter the assistant->user stream. Tool messages now include: role: "tool", metadata headers (tool_id, tool_version), and a content_type header derived from the tool schema (text/plain, application/json, application/x-rl). We also updated streaming to emit an initial metadata event for tool messages so clients can render incremental structured output.

Compatibility notes:
- Backwards compatible defaults retained for hosts not using new semantics. Enable with header "x-redwood-openai-compat: tool_choice_v2".
- Edge cases where downstream consumers relied on previous flat message strings may need small client updates to consume metadata envelopes.

Testing & CI:
- Added unit tests for schema mapping, property conflict resolution, and tool_choice tie-breaking logic.
- End-to-end Python SDK integration tests exercising streaming + tool-calling were added.
- Fixed a flaky streaming test by increasing the event flush timeout and improving test harness isolation.

Rollout plan: staged behind a feature flag for 2 weeks, telemetry will track mapping warnings and ambiguous tool resolutions. We will then flip default if no user-facing regressions are observed.

Checklist:
- [x] Spec doc update (redwood/openai_compat/spec.md)
- [x] Runtime changes (redwood/rt/streaming.py, redwood/openai_compat/handler.py)
- [x] SDK changes (python & sdk-typescript wrappers)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Release notes prepared

References: Linear ENG-1124 (tool-calling spec), ENG-1198 (streaming stability), related PRs pr-34211 and pr-34785 for prior tool_choice work.

release_notes: Standardized OpenAI-compatible tool calling: deterministic tool_choice resolution, robust schema mapping, and structured tool message metadata for streaming clients. Opt-in via header before wide rollout.
